text: This is LeadLoop: an AI sales agent that sells data. SerpApi finds the buyers, SerpApi builds the data, and the agent closes the deal.

Here's how it's built. Four SerpApi engines, Google Jobs, Search, News and Maps, sit behind a cached client. FastAPI streams the agent's work as server-sent events. Groq writes with strict JSON schemas, with Gemini as fallback. And every deal runs as its own LangGraph state machine.
It qualifies the lead, builds a sample, and drafts the pitch. Then it stops: before any email goes out, it calls interrupt and waits for me. State is saved in SQLite, so it can resume days later.
Let's run it. Step one: discover. Nine live SerpApi searches, across India and the US, stream in. Groq reads the news headlines, then drops job boards, competitors and big enterprises.
Every lead gets an intent score, with a reason for each point.
Step two: I start a deal. Groq qualifies the lead, and SerpApi's Google Maps engine builds a ten-row sample. Step three: the graph pauses for my approval.
I approve, and it goes out over SMTP: a sandbox inbox here, Brevo in production.
Step four: negotiation. The model reads each reply, but never picks a price. A pricing engine in code does: a discount ladder with a hard floor. And the deal closes.
This deal closed at ₹3,200. With modest conversion rates, a hundred leads bring in about ₹4,800. That takes just thirty-nine searches on SerpApi, and zero AI cost.
say: This deal closed at three thousand two hundred rupees. With modest conversion rates, a hundred leads bring in about four thousand eight hundred rupees. That takes just thirty-nine searches on Serp API, and zero AI cost.

text: And the time saved, measured in this recording: finding and qualifying leads takes a couple of minutes, not hours. Over ninety-nine percent of the work is automated, and I still approve every email.
That's LeadLoop. Search data in, closed deals out, with a human in the loop. Thank you!
